name: BNO055
title: Intelligent 9-axis absolute orientation sensor
summary: The BNO055 combines a three-axis accelerometer, a three-axis gyroscope, a three-axis magnetometer and a Cortex-M0+ microcontroller running sensor fusion in one 28-pin LGA. It outputs raw sensor data or fused orientation as quaternions and Euler angles, plus linear acceleration, gravity and heading, over I2C, HID-I2C or UART. Sensors run from 2.4 V to 3.6 V and the interface from 1.7 V to 3.6 V, from -40 °C to +85 °C.

pins.name: nBOOT_LOAD_PIN
pins.function: Boot loader select, active low. Held low through reset or power-on, the part starts in boot loader mode; otherwise it starts the application. A 10 kΩ pull-up to VDDIO holds it high in the I2C, UART and HID-I2C connections.

pins.name: BL_IND
pins.function: Boot loader indicator output. DNC in every interface mode of the pin function list.

pins.name: nRESET

circuits.title: I2C connection
circuits.description: The BNO055 wired as an I2C slave: PS1 and PS0 grounded select standard or fast I2C. COM0 and COM1 carry SDA and SCL, each pulled up to VDDIO by RPULL; COM3 is the address select line (high 0x29, low 0x28) and COM2 is grounded. VDD has 100 nF and VDDIO 120 nF to ground, CAP has 1 µF. nBOOT_LOAD_PIN is held high by 10 kΩ so the part starts its application; nRESET has an optional 10 kΩ pull-up. INT and BL_IND go to the host, SWDIO and SWCLK to an optional debugger, and XIN32/XOUT32 to an optional external oscillator.
notes: GND and GNDIO are one ground net.

circuits.title: UART connection
circuits.description: The BNO055 wired for UART: PS1 tied to VDDIO and PS0 grounded select the UART interface. COM0 is TX and COM1 is RX, with no pull-ups; COM2 and COM3 are grounded. Supply decoupling (100 nF on VDD, 120 nF on VDDIO, 1 µF on CAP), the 10 kΩ nBOOT_LOAD_PIN pull-up, the optional 10 kΩ nRESET pull-up and the INT, BL_IND, debugger and oscillator lines match the I2C hook-up.
notes: GND and GNDIO are one ground net.

circuits.title: HID-I2C connection
circuits.description: The BNO055 wired for HID over I2C: PS0 tied to VDDIO and PS1 grounded select the HID-I2C protocol, slave address 0x40. COM0 and COM1 carry SDA and SCL with RPULL pull-ups to VDDIO; COM2 and COM3 are grounded. Decoupling, boot and reset pull-ups and the INT, BL_IND, debugger and oscillator lines match the I2C hook-up.
notes: GND and GNDIO are one ground net.

circuits.title: External 32 kHz crystal oscillator
circuits.description: A 32.768 kHz crystal between XIN32 and XOUT32, each pin loaded with 22 pF to ground. With CLK_SEL set the BNO055 runs from this crystal instead of its internal clock.
notes: Typical crystal voltage amplitude is around 500 to 700 mV.

operation.text: A system in package holding a 14-bit three-axis accelerometer, a 16-bit three-axis gyroscope (up to ±2000 °/s), a three-axis magnetometer and a 32-bit Cortex-M0+ processor that executes Bosch fusion firmware, all inside a 28-pin LGA of 3.8 mm × 5.2 mm × 1.1 mm. It talks over I2C or UART; the I2C port can run the HID-I2C protocol so the part acts as a Windows 8.0/8.1 sensor hub.

VDD feeds the internal sensors; VDDIO feeds the microcontroller and the digital interfaces. VDD must reach its level before VDDIO is switched on, or together with it. Apart from that the two rails may sit at any levels relative to each other inside their ranges.

A power-on reset loads the register defaults and starts the part in CONFIG mode. It runs at every power-up, on a low pulse of at least 20 ns on nRESET, or when RST_SYS in SYS_TRIGGER is set. Start-up from off to config mode takes 400 ms typical; a reset completes into config mode after 650 ms typical.

PWR_MODE selects normal, low power or suspend; normal is the start-up default. In normal mode every sensor the chosen operating mode needs stays on, and the register map and microcontroller peripherals run continuously. The invalid code 11b should not be written.

After a set time without motion (5 s by default) the part drops to low power mode with only the accelerometer running; an any-motion event wakes it back to normal mode. Entry uses the no-motion interrupt settings, wake-up the any-motion settings, and INT can also signal the host. Defaults are tuned for this; a system reset through RST_SYS restores them. In this mode only the no-motion and any-motion interrupts work (not high-g or slow motion), and the mode needs an operating mode that uses the accelerometer.
All sensors and the microcontroller sleep and the register map stops updating. Writing PWR_MODE brings the part out.

OPR_MODE picks which sensors run and which outputs are computed. Sensors the mode does not need are suspended. CONFIGMODE is the default after power-on. Switching from CONFIGMODE to another mode takes 7 ms; switching back takes 19 ms. In any mode the data registers follow the selected units and the axis remap.

Output data read zero and fusion stops. This is the only mode in which every writable register accepts changes, except the interrupt registers (INT_EN, INT_MSK) and OPR_MODE, which can be written in any mode. Another mode must be chosen to read sensor data.

ACCONLY, MAGONLY and GYROONLY run one sensor and suspend the others, so the part behaves like a single discrete sensor. ACCMAG, ACCGYRO and MAGGYRO run two sensors; AMG runs all three. Sensor settings made in config mode are kept.

Fusion modes compute orientation, as quaternions or as Euler angles (roll, pitch, yaw), and split measured acceleration into linear acceleration and the gravity vector. Absolute modes reference the earth's magnetic field and so find magnetic north; relative modes give a heading that depends on the starting position. In fusion modes the sensors use the defaults of the power-on configuration table and are set by the part itself. Background calibration of all sensors always runs and cannot be turned off.

Accelerometer data correct gyroscope drift; during motion they are set aside and pitch and roll come from the gyroscope, so long vibration or continuous movement can make pitch and roll drift. Distorted magnetometer data are dropped automatically, which can make heading drift as in IMU mode. The algorithm targets human motion: sustained large accelerations, such as hard cornering or long braking in a vehicle, can be mistaken for gravity, so such uses should be tested.
Relative orientation from accelerometer and gyroscope; fast, with a high output rate (100 Hz).

Measures the earth's field to find geographic direction. Heading uses the horizontal field components, which needs the gravity direction, so gravity and field are used together. Accuracy depends on a stable surrounding field; because device fields are usually much larger than the earth's, this mode needs calibration.

Like IMU, but rotation is sensed from the magnetometer's changing orientation in the field instead of the gyroscope. It draws less current than IMU and has no gyroscope drift, but accuracy depends on a stable surrounding field. No magnetometer calibration is needed or offered.

NDOF fuses all three sensors into absolute orientation with a high output rate and good tolerance of magnetic distortion. Its fast magnetometer calibration gives quick calibration and better accuracy at slightly higher current than NDOF_FMC_OFF, which is the same mode with fast magnetometer calibration off.

AXIS_MAP_CONFIG and AXIS_MAP_SIGN reassign and invert the output axes to suit how the part is mounted. The default axes follow the package: X and Y in the package plane, Z out of the top face, the same frame for accelerometer, gyroscope and magnetometer.

ACC_Config, GYR_Config_0/1 and MAG_Config (register page 1) set range, bandwidth, rate and power mode in non-fusion modes. In fusion modes these settings are controlled by the part and the user's choices are restricted.

UNIT_SEL picks m/s² or mg, dps or rps, degrees or radians, °C or °F, and Windows or Android orientation convention. Raw sensor registers hold uncompensated data in non-fusion modes and compensated data in fusion modes; Euler, quaternion, linear acceleration and gravity outputs exist only in fusion modes. Linear acceleration usually cannot be integrated into velocity or position: without other sensors the error outgrows the signal within a second.
A burst (multi-byte) read is shadowed so the LSB and MSB of every axis come from the same sample. With single-byte reads the MSB can change between reading the LSB and the MSB.

Offset and radius registers can be read once fully calibrated and stored by the host, then written back after a power-on reset to get correct orientation at once. Read them in CONFIG_MODE after full calibration. To restore: enter CONFIG_MODE, write the offsets and radii, then select a fusion mode. Wrong offsets can give unreliable orientation even at calibration level 3. Once the internal calibration runs again it overwrites the stored profile.

INT is latched and goes high on a rising-edge event; it stays high until the host sets RST_INT in SYS_TRIGGER. INT_EN enables each interrupt, INT_MSK routes it to the pin (without the mask only INT_STA updates), and INT_STA records occurrences and clears when read.

Available from software 03.14. ACC_BSX_DRDY, MAG_DRDY and GYR_DRDY flag new accelerometer, magnetometer and gyroscope data at each sensor's rate in non-fusion modes. In fusion modes ACC_BSX_DRDY flags new fused data at the primary sensor rate. INT stays high until reset or read; if several interrupts arrive before that, INT pulses low and high again.

SMNM selects slow-motion or no-motion. Slow motion fires when the slope on any enabled axis stays above ACC_NM_THRES for slo_no_mot_dur<1:0>+1 samples. No motion fires when the slope on all enabled axes stays below the threshold for the delay set by slo_no_mot_dur, in 1 s timer ticks. Axes are chosen with the AM/NM axis bits shared with any-motion.

The slope between successive samples is compared with ACC_AM_THRES; the interrupt sets when any enabled axis exceeds it for AM_DUR+1 points and clears when all enabled axes stay below for AM_DUR+1 points, unless latched.

Fires when the magnitude on any enabled axis (HG_X/Y/Z_AXIS) exceeds ACC_HG_THRES for the ACC_HG_DURATION delay, and resets when all enabled axes stay below it for the same delay. Enabled by ACC_HIGH_G in INT_EN; status in INT_STA.

Fires when the rate magnitude on any enabled axis exceeds HR_<axis>_Threshold for the GYR_DUR_<axis> delay; resets when all enabled axes fall below the threshold minus the hysteresis. HR_FILT selects filtered or unfiltered data. Enabled by GYR_HIGH_RATE in INT_EN.

The slope between successive rate samples is compared with GYR_AM_THRES; the interrupt sets when any enabled axis exceeds it for (Slope Samples+1)×4 samples and clears after the same count below, unless latched. AM_FILT selects filtered or unfiltered data.

At start-up the part checks the chip IDs of its three sensors and runs a memory self-test of the microcontroller; results land in ST_RESULT (1 = pass). The host can start a built-in self-test of the three sensors from config mode by setting Self_Test in SYS_TRIGGER; other functions pause meanwhile. SYS_STATUS shows 'executing selftest' and changes only on failure. After about 400 ms SYS_ERR reads 0 on success or 3 on failure, and ST_RESULT then shows which sensor failed.
The boot loader runs at every reset and power-up and checks nBOOT_LOAD_PIN: low enters boot loader mode, otherwise the application starts. The pin should be connected as in the connection diagrams.

Hold the device still in six different positions for a few seconds each, moving slowly between them, with each of the x, y and z axes perpendicular at least once. CALIB_STAT shows progress. Steps are repeated after every power-on reset.
Hold the device still in one position for a few seconds; CALIB_STAT shows progress.

The steps correct hard-iron distortion. In COMPASS, M4G and NDOF_FMC_OFF, move the device randomly (for example tracing a figure 8 in the air) until CALIB_STAT reads fully calibrated. NDOF needs fewer movements, at slightly higher current.

A 3×3 matrix multiplies the magnetometer data before fusion to correct soft-magnetic material near the sensor. It starts as the identity matrix. Generating it, ideally with Helmholtz coils or less precisely in the earth's field, is the customer's task.

All communication is register reads and writes on 8-bit registers in two pages; PAGE_ID (0x07) reads and selects the active register page, with page 0 active after power-on. Writes to read-only registers are ignored; trigger bits are write-only and read 0. Fully reserved registers should be left alone and reserved bits masked off.
PS1 and PS0 choose standard/fast I2C (00), HID over I2C (01) or UART (10); 11 is reserved and the pins must not float. COM0 to COM3 change role with the interface.

Standard and fast mode up to 400 kHz, 7-bit addressing only, compatible with I2C specification UM10204 Rev. 03. The part stretches the clock. Address 0x29 with COM3 high (default, internal pull-up), 0x28 with COM3 low, 0x40 in HID-I2C. SDA and SCL need external pull-ups to VDDIO. A write is address, register, data; a read writes the register address, then a repeated start and read with auto-increment, ended by a NACK and stop. A read without a new address restarts at the last address written (0x00 by default). A START followed at once by a STOP is not recognised.

115200 bps, 8N1, up to 128 bytes per read or write. Commands start with 0xAA; a write is acknowledged with 0xEE and a status byte, a read returns 0xBB, a length and the data, or 0xEE and an error status. A command with a wrong start byte gets no reply. Successive characters must arrive within 30 ms.
A standard protocol for HID devices on I2C, so generic host drivers can use the sensor; the host reads a report descriptor from the part at start-up and exchanges reports and events defined there.

The part runs from an internal 32 kHz clock by default, which can deviate by up to +3 %. Setting CLK_SEL in SYS_TRIGGER (preferably in config mode) switches to an external 32.768 kHz crystal on XIN32/XOUT32, recommended for best performance. The part checks the crystal signal and falls back to the internal clock, clearing CLK_SEL, if it is bad. Configuring the crystal and starting takes at least about 600 ms. Poll ST_MAIN_CLK in SYS_CLK_STATUS until it clears, then read CLK_SEL: set means the crystal is running. With the internal clock XIN32 and XOUT32 can stay open.

Moisture sensitivity level 1 per IPC/JEDEC J-STD-020E; lead-free reflow with peak temperature up to 260 °C. The MEMS structure tolerates shocks of several thousand g, which a hammer blow or a drop onto a hard surface can exceed. ESD protection reaches 2 kV HBM, but normal CMOS precautions apply. Terminal voltages must stay within the supply range and unused inputs must be tied to a defined level.

RoHS compliant (2011/65/EU with 2015/863/EU), halogen-free, MSL1. Shipped in a cardboard box. Second-source LGA packages may differ in chemical content and internal structure but have identical package parameters.
